title: Laravel Octane Performance: Benchmarking and Optimization Guide
meta_description: Maximize Laravel Octane performance in 2026. Comprehensive benchmarking guide comparing Swoole vs RoadRunner, with real optimization techniques that deliver 10x throughput gains.
excerpt: Laravel Octane supercharges PHP applications by keeping them in memory between requests—eliminating bootstrap overhead and dramatically increasing throughput. This guide benchmarks Octane on Swoole and RoadRunner, identifies the most impactful optimizations, and gives you the configuration playbook for production-grade performance.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: 8-12x throughput gains with zero application code changes. Explain the bootstrap problem Octane solves. Preview: architecture, server comparison, benchmarks, optimizations, gotchas.
content_structure.section_1: How Octane works: application booted once, kept in memory (Swoole coroutines or RoadRunner workers), requests handled without PHP-FPM fork overhead, shared state implications.
content_structure.section_2: Swoole vs RoadRunner: Swoole (PHP extension, coroutine-based, faster raw throughput, complex setup), RoadRunner (Go binary, easier setup, slightly lower ceiling, WebSocket support). Decision matrix.
content_structure.section_3: Benchmark methodology and results: tested on 2-core/4GB VPS. Metrics: req/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory under load. Baseline PHP-FPM vs Octane/Swoole vs Octane/RoadRunner vs FrankenPHP.
content_structure.section_4: Top 10 optimizations: route caching, config caching, eager loading elimination (N+1 detection with Telescope), Redis for cache/queue/session, DB connection pooling, Octane table for shared state, removing unused service providers.
content_structure.section_5: Memory leak patterns: static properties persisting between requests, event listener accumulation, singleton abuse, Eloquent model state pollution. Detection and fix strategies.
content_structure.conclusion: Octane deployment checklist. CTA: Download the Laravel Octane Production Configuration Template.
content_structure.faq_section: Q1: Is Octane safe to use in production? Q2: How do I detect memory leaks in Octane? Q3: Does Octane work with Livewire? Q4: Can I use Octane on shared hosting?

title: API-First Laravel: Headless and Decoupled Architecture Patterns
meta_description: Master API-first and headless Laravel architecture in 2026. Learn decoupled patterns, API versioning, and how to power multiple frontends from a single Laravel backend.
excerpt: Building API-first with Laravel unlocks a powerful architectural advantage: one backend powers your web app, mobile app, third-party integrations, and public API simultaneously. This guide covers the headless patterns, versioning strategies, and authentication approaches that production teams rely on.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: one backend, unlimited consumers. Define API-first and the architectural benefits. Preview: API design principles, auth comparison, versioning, performance, testing.
content_structure.section_1: Why API-first: mobile app parity, third-party integration readiness, frontend framework freedom, microservices migration path, public API monetization. Real examples.
content_structure.section_2: API design with Laravel Resources: transforming Eloquent models, sparse fieldsets, relationship inclusion (JSON:API patterns), consistent error responses, pagination standards.
content_structure.section_3: Auth strategies: Sanctum (SPA + token auth, simpler), Passport (full OAuth2, for public APIs), JWT (stateless, for microservices). Decision guide for each use case.
content_structure.section_4: Versioning patterns: URL versioning (/api/v1/), header versioning, content negotiation. Deprecation strategies, changelog maintenance, client communication.
content_structure.section_5: Performance and testing: response caching (with cache-control headers), eager loading API responses, Pest feature tests for API endpoints, Scribe for auto-generated OpenAPI docs.
content_structure.conclusion: API-first Laravel implementation checklist. CTA: Download the Laravel API Design Standards Template.
